name: Heartswood
summary: In northwestern Ashenvale, Heartswood is cut from a tree rooted among the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. The tree grew where two ancient lovers died, and its wood draws succubi when warlocks seek to summon them.

sections.title: A Monument to Devotion
sections.body: Among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale, a peculiar tree took root. Legend says Anathera and Latherion, two lovers, fell side by side there during the War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. The Heartswood tree grew from the earth where they died. Even now, wood cut from it carries the memory of their devotion. Those who study emotional and spiritual bonds are curious about it.

sections.title: A Tool of Subjugation
sections.body: Heartswood draws the attention of succubi, demons drawn to passion, longing, and emotional exploitation. Human and gnome warlocks learning from Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind seek the rare timber to make a ritual lure. Its resonance with the lovers' sacrifice can bait a succubus across the Nether and draw her into a summoning circle. There, the practitioner can bind her to their will.

faq.answer: Heartswood is wood from a tree that grew in Ashenvale's Ruins of Ordil'Aran, where two ancient night elf lovers died together during the War of the Ancients.

Anathera and Latherion were lovers who fought side by side during the War of the Ancients. They fell in battle, and their final embrace nourished the earth where the Heartswood tree grew as a lasting sign of their devotion.
Succubi are demons drawn to desire and emotional manipulation. Warlocks use Heartswood's resonance with undying love as bait to tempt a succubus into the physical world and summon her.
Heartswood comes from the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in the northwestern Ashenvale forest, near the border of Darkshore.

angles.text: For Alliance warlocks, securing Heartswood is a rite of passage directed by Gakin the Darkbinder. Its resonance provides the emotional bait needed to compel and bind a succubus minion.
As a night elf, you may see the tree as a sacred memorial to those who fell in the War of the Ancients. Warlocks and cultists who cut its wood offend the memory of fallen ancestors.
